messages:
Lena: Heads-up, ran a quick speculative-prefill pass against redwood-7b-quant on our customer-like prompt set. Latency win looks good (~2.1x tokens/s) but noticing stop-token handling regressions and occasional early truncation.

Devon: Oof. stop-token issues are annoying. Do you have a minimal repro or run command?

Lena: run:```
bench run --model redwood-7b-quant-int8 --speculative-prefill true --prefill-threshold 0.25 --micro-batch 16 --sample-seed 777 --prompts small-cust-200 --record-raw true
```Quick metrics: tokens/s 2400 vs baseline 1150, p50 latency 28ms -> 13ms, stop-truncation-rate 1.9% (baseline 0.1%), early-eos avg position -2.4 tokens.

bench-bot: job complete - tokens_per_sec:2400, baseline_tokens_per_sec:1150, p50_latency_ms:13, stop_trunc_pct:1.9, avg_eos_delta:-2.4

Priya: Are these deterministic? quant kernels sometimes flip order with micro-batches which can alter kv-cache writes. Also which quant backend? FBGEMM or custom int8?

Lena: Using qbackend=fastq (custom int8). I pinned seed but not kernel_order_lock. Logs show a few kv-checksum mismatches on ~0.8% of steps.

Devon: If kv checksums differ, could be cache alignment bug. But stop-token regressions might also be from speculation picking a high-prob english punctuation early. Did you compare token probs around EOS?

Lena: Yes — mean prob(eos) at true-eos step increases by 0.12 absolute in speculative runs, so spec path is inflating eos mass. Entropy drops ~0.15 nats avg.

Priya: Two hypotheses: 1) speculative prefill logic merges prefix logits in a way that biases EOS for quantized logits, 2) quant rounding increases softmax sharpness, and specifier compounds it by committing earlier.

Devon: Practical checks: re-run with
- qbackend=fp16 (no quant) + spec on
- spec off + quant on (to isolate quant)&
- spec with higher threshold (0.4/0.6)
- enable kernel_order_lock

Lena: Agreed. I'll run that matrix. Also adding an experiment: keep spec path but clamp eos-prob to baseline smoothing factor at post-softmax for punctuation/EOS tokens only. Quick patch to try.

ops-bot: quota note - running all jobs will consume ~18 node-hours across bench cluster, estimated cost ~2.4k credits. Proceed?

Priya: Low-cost sanity: first run q=fp16+spec on one node to see if eos inflation persists. If it doesn't, quant is the smoking gun.

Lena: Kicked off fp16+spec quick job: job-176421a. Will post outputs.

bench-bot: job-176421a started (fp16+spec). ETA ~22m.

Devon: Also capture raw logits for first 50 prompts and diff EOS logit trajectories. If those diverge early that's telling.

Lena: noted. saving raw logits + per-token entropy and token-indexed eos_prob.

Priya: If quant + spec persists as issue, let's try two mitigations: a) spec fallback when eos_prob > 0.4 OR b) modest temp bump (1.05) on spec path to flatten softmax. Measure impact on both latency and stop-truncation.

Lena: I'll add both. Tentative schedule: quick fp16 run -> analyze -> if quant likely, run quant+kernel-lock + clamp + temp bump. Expect full matrix in ~6 hours.

Devon: Good. please annotate runs with git sha and model artifact id. Also add a small human eval set for outputs where early-eos occurred to check downstream quality.

Lena: will attach sha c4d2f9 and model redwood-7b-quant-int8:v2026-03-20. Posting updates in this thread as jobs finish.

Priya: Thanks. If we confirm it's quant+spec synergy, we should default speculative prefill off for quantized-only shards until we have a mitigation.

Devon: +1. Could also gate specifier with a quick per-request entropy check in the runtime as a temporary safety.

Lena: Good ideas. Will report back with numbers.

bench-bot: job-176421a complete - fp16+spec: tokens_per_sec:2380, stop_trunc_pct:0.12, avg_eos_delta:-0.05, p50_latency_ms:14

Lena: fp16+spec run shows eos inflation gone (stop_trunc down to baseline). Looks like quant path is amplifying the issue. Moving to quant+kernel-lock job next.

Priya: Great signal. Prioritize kernel_lock + small temp bump test to see if we can keep spec perf while avoiding regressions.

Devon: Thanks Lena — this is a solid triage flow.
